options: The frequency stays 250 Hz and the wavelength stretches to 6 m
The frequency rises to keep the wavelength fixed
Both frequency and wavelength stay the same
The frequency falls because water is denser

subtopics.title: Sonar — Timing Plus the Wave Equation

questions.question: A sonar echo returns to the ship after 1,2 s through seawater at 1 500 m·s⁻¹. The depth is:
options: 900 m — halve the 1 800 m round trip

questions.question: The wavelength of a 25 kHz sonar pulse in seawater at 1 500 m·s⁻¹ is:
options: 0,06 m — λ = 1 500 ÷ 25 000, with no factor of two anywhere
0,03 m, after halving for the round trip

questions.question: The factor of two in sonar work belongs to:
options: The depth calculation only — halving is for round trips, never wavelengths

questions.question: Sonar uses 25 kHz rather than a foghorn's 250 Hz because:
options: Higher frequencies travel faster in water
The short 0,06 m wavelength reflects crisply off small objects a 6 m wave would flow past

questions.question: Ultrasound is sound with a frequency:
options: Above the human hearing ceiling of about 20 000 Hz

questions.question: A bat calling at 85 kHz in air produces a wavelength of:
options: 0,004 m — 340 ÷ 85 000, about the size of a moth

questions.question: A moth hangs 2,55 m from the bat. The bat's squeak returns after:
options: 0,015 s — the 5,1 m round trip divided by 340 m·s⁻¹

questions.question: A dolphin clicking at 50 kHz in seawater at 1 500 m·s⁻¹ makes waves of:
options: 0,03 m — three centimetres, fine enough to single out one fish

subtopics.title: The Ear's Limits, and Ultrasound in Medicine

questions.question: The human ear is most sensitive:
options: At the very top of its range
In the middle of its range, around the frequencies of speech
At the very bottom of its range

questions.question: A 17 kHz ringtone pierces a teenager's ears but the adult teacher hears nothing because:
options: Adults ignore high sounds by habit
The ringtone is too soft for adults
Age and noise damage erode the top of the hearing range first

questions.question: An ultrasound scanner locates a tissue boundary by:
options: Timing the reflected pulse and converting time to depth with the echo rule
Measuring how loud the echo is only
Heating the tissue and measuring the glow

questions.question: Ultrasound is safe for scanning an unborn baby because it is:
options: Absorbed completely by the mother's skin
A mechanical pressure wave, not ionising radiation, so it cannot damage cells

questions.question: You count 5 s between the flash and the thunder. The storm is about:
Storm counting uses no factor of two because:
options: The thunder made a one-way trip — halving belongs only to echoes that return
Thunder is too loud to halve
The factor of two only applies underwater

questions.question: Louder thunder crosses town:
options: At the same 340 m·s⁻¹ — the speed belongs to the air

questions.question: A wave reflects usefully off an object when the object is:
options: About the size of the wavelength or bigger

questions.question: The bat squeaks at 85 kHz rather than at speaking pitch because:
options: Its 4 mm waves bounce off a moth that metre-long waves would flow straight around

questions.question: To detect ever smaller targets, an echolocator must:
options: Send shorter waves — which means higher frequency, since the medium fixes the speed

questions.question: An ultrasound scanner is like a torch because it:
options: Uses a bright lamp inside the probe
Warms the body as it scans
Builds a picture from waves bounced back by what they strike — sound instead of light

questions.question: An echo inside the body returns after 0,000 06 s with sound at 1 500 m·s⁻¹. The boundary lies:
options: 4,5 cm deep — 1 500 × 0,000 06 gives 9 cm out-and-back, then halve

questions.question: Which is NOT a genuine use of ultrasound?
options: Finding hidden cracks inside welded steel
